paragraphs: Hillel and Yehudah, Gamliel’s sons. Semachot, beginning of chapter 8: an incident with Yehudah and Hillel, Gamliel’s sons, who entered—in Tosefta Shabbat chapter 8, they entered Kavul; thus they are those mentioned shortly below, and neither ben Zakkai nor Rabbi Tarfon is mentioned—to ben Zakkai in Babylonia. In newer Talmud editions another reading is “to Rabbi Tarfon in Kevel.” The townspeople drew channels of wine and oil before them. Which Gamliel this is requires examination. If Gamliel of Yavneh, who saw Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai, he was nevertheless then called Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai, for he was called ben Zakkai in his youth. Thus this should be Gamliel the Elder; requires examination. Perhaps for this reason newer editions corrected it to entering Rabbi Tarfon’s house, making them Gamliel of Yavneh’s sons (see shortly below). Moreover, who brought ben Zakkai to Babylonia, since Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai was in the Land of Israel? Hillel and Yehudah, Rabbi Gamliel’s sons: chapter Makom Shenahagu, 51a. They entered to bathe in Kavul and were told that two brothers do not customarily bathe together. They went out in golden sandals on the Sabbath in Biri: Tosefta Moed Katan chapter 2. Yuchasin writes that Gamliel, son of our holy master, had two sons, Hillel and Yehudah. Yehudah was called Rabbi Yehudah Nesia. Asarah Maamarot, Chikkur Din,part 2,chapter 19, likewise says so; see Yad Yehudah,section 42. This Hillel said in Avot chapter 2, “Do not separate from the community” (see Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel the Elder).
